newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets details of 3.5 bln yuan rail bond issue.
newsitem.headline: China sets details of 3.5 bln yuan rail bond issue.

text.p: China unveiled details of its planned 3.5 billion yuan ($421 million) railway bond issue on Friday, saying that two billion yuan would have a three-year maturity while the remainder would be five years.
The official China Securities newspaper said the three-year debt would carry interest of 11 percent and the five-year debt 12 percent.
It said the debt was rated AAA by domestic rating agency Cheng Xin Rating.
The newspaper did not say what the funds would be used for but China has previously said it plans to invest 34.4 billion yuan in railway construction projects this year, up from 32 billion in 1996.

The official China Daily quoted Vice-Minister of Railways Sun Yongfu as saying the funds would be used to upgrade the newly installed Beijing-Shenzhen service as well as the Chengdu-Kunming and Nanning-Kunming routes in the southwest and Datong-Qinhuangdao, a major coal carrying route in the northeast.
The bonds would be issued from January 20. ($1 = 8.3 yuan) --Beijing newsroom (8610) 6532-1921
